What's more remarkable is the fact that the opah is a deep water fish, where the colder water forces most species to conserve energy by reducing extraneous movement. How the opah manages to stay warm:

...produces heat through the constant “flapping” of wing-like pectoral fins and minimizes heat loss through a series of counter-current heat exchangers within its gills.

This allows it to take on characteristics of fish in warmer water, such as a large heart, big eyes, and higher physiological performance than is otherwise possible in deep water. The distinction here is also that it is fully warm-blooded, while some fish (e.g. tuna) can actually warm up certain parts of the body (see source article). So, the fact that fish can produce enough heat to keep certain organs warm isn't in itself overly unique; being able to do so for the entire body is, since that was previously thought to be limited to birds and mammals.
